import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/iris.csv')

# Set the visual style for the plots
sns.set_theme(style="ticks")

# Create a custom color palette
palette = {
    'setosa': '#1f77b4',
    'versicolor': '#ff7f0e',
    'virginica': '#2ca02c'
}

# Create the pairplot
# A pairplot shows pairwise relationships between variables and is colored by species.
# The diagonal shows the distribution of each feature for each species (using KDE).
g = sns.pairplot(
    df,
    hue='species',
    palette=palette,
    diag_kind='kde',
    plot_kws={'alpha': 0.7, 's': 40, 'edgecolor': 'k'},
    diag_kws={'fill': True, 'alpha': 0.5}
)

# Add a descriptive title to the overall figure
g.fig.suptitle("Pairwise Relationships and Distributions in the Iris Dataset", y=1.02, fontsize=16)

# Improve individual axis labels for clarity
for i, col in enumerate(df.columns[:-1]):
    g.axes[i, 0].set_ylabel(col.replace('_', ' ').title() + ' (cm)')
    g.axes[-1, i].set_xlabel(col.replace('_', ' ').title() + ' (cm)')

# Adjust legend title
g._legend.set_title("Species")

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
